problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+x{y}^{′}+y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+x{y}^{′}+y=0,\,y(1)=2,\,{y}^{′}(1)=-5,\,x>0.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Cauchy-Euler Equations: Characteristic Equations With Complex Roots

feedback.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+t{y}^{′}+2y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+t{y}^{′}+2y=0,\,y(1)=0,\,{y}^{′}(1)=1,\,t>0.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(1)=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
0={c}_{1}.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=1,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\sqrt{2}\,{t}^{-1}({c}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)-{c}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute ${y}^{′}(1)=1$ and ${c}_{1}=0$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =\sqrt{2}{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t).
$$
